source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Decide what evidence should be observed or measured to make sense of changes in an experiment.
node_labels: What counts as a scientific question or test

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Evidence: the amount of oil added, not whether the puri puffed.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Record everything from memory after the experiment; notes during it are unnecessary.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Whether the puri puffed cannot count as evidence because it is only a yes/no observation.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: No smoke or splatter means there is no evidence to record.

intelligence.enrichment: To interpret an experiment, choose observable or measurable results; some results may be yes/no, some may be numbers, and notes can include what is seen or sensed such as puffing, splatter, smell, or smoke. Chosen observations and measurements turn changes in the experiment into evidence that can be compared. The learner chooses observable or measurable results, including yes/no observations, numbers, and experiment notes, as evidence for interpreting changes. Writing down what was changed is enough evidence, even if no result is observed or measured.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Exploring the inquisitive mind. The student must decide: Decide what evidence should be observed or measured to make sense of changes in an experiment. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.options, not typed into part text.
